```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

movies <- read_csv("data/movies.csv")
```

```{r}
#| cache: true

# Split comma-separated genres into one genre per row
movies_clean <- movies |>
  separate_longer_delim(genre, delim = ", ")
```

```{r}
# Plot histogram of critic scores in 5-point bins
movies |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tomatoMeter)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Rotten Tomatoes Critic Scores",
    subtitle = "Across 29,783 films",
    x = "Tomatometer Score",
    y = "Count"
  )
```

```{r}
# Drop zero scores, compute gap, and summarize genres with at least 100 rows
movies_gap <- movies_clean |>
  filter(tomatoMeter != 0, audienceScore != 0) |>
  mutate(gap = tomatoMeter - audienceScore)

movies_summary <- movies_gap |>
  summarize(
    mean_gap = mean(gap),
    n = n(),
    .by = genre
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 100) |>
  arrange(mean_gap)
```

```{r}
# Plot horizontal bars ordered from most audience-favored to most critic-favored
movies_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_gap, y = fct_reorder(genre, mean_gap))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Critics Favor Horror and Documentaries; Audiences Prefer Action",
    subtitle = "Mean Tomatometer minus Audience Score for genres with at least 100 films",
    x = "Average Gap (Tomatometer - Audience Score)",
    y = "Genre"
  )
```

```{r}
# Filter to the 8 live-action Spider-Man films, assign actor by title pattern, and sort by release date
spiderman <- movies |>
  filter(
    title %in% c(
      "Spider-Man",
      "Spider-Man 2",
      "Spider-Man 3",
      "The Amazing Spider-Man",
      "The Amazing Spider-Man 2",
      "Spider-Man: Homecoming",
      "Spider-Man: Far From Home",
      "Spider-Man: No Way Home"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    actor = case_when(
      str_detect(title, "Amazing") ~ "Andrew Garfield",
      str_detect(title, ":") ~ "Tom Holland",
      .default = "Tobey Maguire"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(releaseDateTheaters)

# Reshape both score columns so ggplot draws two lines with a legend
spiderman |>
  mutate(title = fct_inorder(title)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(tomatoMeter, audienceScore),
    names_to = "score_type",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    score_type = if_else(
      score_type == "tomatoMeter",
      "Tomatometer (Critics)",
      "Audience Score"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = title, y = score, color = score_type, group = score_type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Audience Scores Climbed Past Critics by the Tom Holland Era",
    subtitle = "Rotten Tomatoes critic and audience scores across live-action Spider-Man films in release order",
    x = "Film (Release Order)",
    y = "Score",
    color = "Rating Source"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
```
